title: Customer threads cartography and low-touch experiments
content:
Working sketch — high-level cartography of customer threads and candidate low-touch experiments (notes + quick proposals).

Source window: tickets + in-app feedback + CSM calls + NPS comments (2026-06 to 2026-08). Pulled raw phrases, consolidated patterns. This is intentionally informal: use as a handoff for eng/product to pick small, measurable probes.

1) Executive summary
- Big theme: customers frequently surface three operational friction areas: inference latency variability, model-compatibility/rollout surprises, and cost-visibility at token/granularity level.
- Near-term goal: define 3 low-effort probes that reduce noise for >30% of recurring tickets in each theme.
- Long-term ask: fold recurring probes into roadmap lanes if they show >20% reduction in ticket volume or measurable revenue retention impact.

2) Raw thread clusters (phrases extracted)
- "spikes in tail latency when sequence len > 1k"
- "we got different outputs after canary, broken prompt behavior"
- "cost for embeddings is opaque — want per-route breakdown"
- "dedicated pool autoscale flaps during midday burst"
- "function calling streaming sometimes truncates"

3) Cartography: mapped touchpoints and frequency (rough counts)
- Serving/runtime: latency spikes, autoscale events, tail p99 variability (35 mentions).
- Deploy/rollouts: model mismatch, canary surprises, mismatch in quantized variants (21 mentions).
- Billing/visibility: surprise invoices, token attribution, per-route cost (18 mentions).
- SDK/UX: streaming truncation, error messages unclear (12 mentions).
- Security/compliance signals (audit logs access requests) (6 mentions).

4) Immediate low-touch experiment candidates (description, how to measure, expected impact, owner)
A. Tail-latency prefix-caching pilot
- Idea: enable ephemeral prefix/KV caching for long-sequence customers with known hot prefixes. Config knob in Console -> per-route toggle.
- Measure: compare p95/p99 token latency and ticket rate for pilot cohort vs control (30 days).
- Expected impact: p99 reduction ~20–40% for affected flows, ticket reduction for latency-related threads ~40% in pilot.
- Owner: Miguel Ortega (SRE) + eng-serving-runtime
- Quick implementation notes: use existing KV cache feature; add telemetry tag and per-route toggle. Low risk.

B. Canary-visibility diff tool (diff of model outputs + prompt fingerprints)
- Idea: small tool that records prompt fingerprint + deterministic metadata during canary and produces a compact diff report (sampled) that CS can attach to ticket.
- Measure: reduction in "unexpected output after canary" threads; speed to root-cause (median time to triage).
- Expected impact: faster triage, fewer rollback cycles; pilot target: reduce repeat canary tickets by 30% within 2 sprints.
- Owner: Anika Bose (Product) + applied-ml
- Notes: prototype could be a lightweight lambda that snapshots inputs/outputs for a sampled percentage (1–5%). Privacy: redact PII; use opt-in per-customer.

C. Per-route cost breakdown beta (console addition)
- Idea: expose a compact per-route cost view (tokens, model variant, cache hits) with an exportable CSV and an alert if route spend grows >25% week-over-week.
- Measure: customer-configured alerts triggered, CS calls avoided, invoice disputes lowered.
- Expected impact: fewer surprise invoices; quicker CS conversations. Pilot metric: reduce billing disputes related to confusion by 50% for participants.
- Owner: Samir Patel (GTM ops) + product-hosted-api

5) Quick wins / playbook items (can be done within a sprint)
- Add a template reply for latency-tail tickets describing sequence-length correlation and ask for payload samples (reduces back-and-forth).
- Tweak streaming error message to include a unique request-id and guidance: "if truncation, include request-id + last-token-index".
- Enable token-cost headers for internal trace mode for top 10 enterprise customers (non-invasive).

6) Risks / open questions
- Data retention and privacy for canary-diff snapshots — need legal sign-off for sampled snapshots.
- Resource contention: enabling per-route cache may increase memory usage on serving nodes; need capacity check.
- Measurement noise: ticket labels are inconsistent; need a short taxonomy exercise with CS triage team (see linked artifact JIRA-CS-4219).

7) Proposed experiment cadence and stop/go criteria
- 30-day pilot windows. Daily telemetry + weekly triage syncs.
- Stop if no signal improvement in primary metric (p99 latency for A, ticket count for B, dispute rate for C) after 2 weeks OR if customers report increased instability.

8) Handoff TODOs and next steps
- Miguel: prototype per-route cache toggle + telemetry tag (ETA: 2 weeks).
- Anika: draft canary-diff minimal schema and privacy checklist, coordinate with legal (ETA: 1 week).
- Samir: sketch console mock for per-route cost breakdown and identify pilot customers (ETA: 1 week).
- CS: identify 6 pilot customers across small/medium/enterprise and collect baseline ticket counts.

9) Notes to self / working thoughts (unstructured)
- Might be useful to combine B + A for customers where output regressions correlate with long sequences (probable).
- Consider an "alias detection" filter in canary-diff so repeated syntactic variants are grouped.
- Cheap UX: add a "why am I being billed more?" inline tooltip that links to per-route breakdown beta.

10) Slack/Jira anchors / reference links (quick)
- Slack: #cs-product-lab thread "latency-cartography" (search).
- JIRA: JIRA-CS-4219 (taxonomy), JIRA-ENG-3378 (cache toggle), JIRA-PROD-2891 (cost-breakdown mock).
- Confluence hub: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/CS/Cartography+Hub

Appendix: raw verbatims sampled (sanitized)
- "We saw a spike at 3pm EST yesterday — generator slowed to a crawl past 800 tokens."
- "Canary output has diverged, but logs don't show which variant ran for these requests."
- "Our finance team wants a CSV we can reconcile with our vendor billing."

-- end sketch --

If this looks useful, I'll fold into a short slide with prioritized bets and ask eng/product for time estimates. Otherwise, mark which probe to pursue first and I'll open the pilot tickets.
